purpose: Define the intended integration boundary through which Aurora AI can use Genesis Engine capabilities without claiming that a working adapter or runtime connection already exists.

aurora_ai: Interpret user intent and formulate proposed engine tasks
Select only registered and authorized Genesis tools
Validate request schema and apply policy/capability checks before invocation
Present progress, errors and results with provenance
Require explicit approval for policy-designated consequential side effects
genesis_engine: Own engine runtime, ECS/world simulation, rendering, assets, build/editor and franchise-factory behavior
Return typed results, errors and artifact provenance
ecosystem_control_plane: Track ownership, versioned contracts, compatibility, security review and exact-SHA evidence
Not implement the Aurora adapter or Genesis runtime

use_cases.name: Natural-language game project creation
use_cases.flow: Aurora intent -> validated project specification -> authorized Genesis project/template/build tools -> typed artifact result

use_cases.name: World and gameplay prototyping
use_cases.flow: Aurora proposal -> schema validation and policy check -> Genesis simulation/editor command -> deterministic engine validation -> result

use_cases.name: Franchise Factory workflow orchestration
use_cases.flow: Aurora proposal -> authorized workflow selection -> Genesis Franchise Factory executor boundary -> artifact/provenance report

use_cases.name: Build, QA and packaging assistance
use_cases.flow: Aurora task plan -> bounded and authorized build/QA tool -> Genesis executor -> logs, status and artifact references

contract_requirements.transport: UNDECIDED. Source inspection found an in-process Python WorkflowEngine with injected Executor, but no established Aurora-to-Genesis transport/API. Select a versioned adapter boundary only after ownership, deployment topology and isolation requirements are resolved.

security_and_authority: Deny by default; Aurora model output is a proposal, not authorization.
Every engine tool call must pass schema validation, policy evaluation and capability authorization.
Mutating, publishing, deleting, deploying, or externally visible actions require approval when policy marks them consequential.
AI inference and asynchronous agent output must not directly mutate deterministic simulation state; changes enter through validated engine commands.
Genesis Engine remains distinct from ShivaCore TCB, A-TownChain consensus, canonical ATC-VM and governance authority.
No ambient credentials or unrestricted network access are granted to tool executors.
verification_gates: Inspect exact source symbols and manifests in both aurora-ai and genesis-engine at pinned SHAs.
Publish and review a versioned adapter/tool contract.
Pass contract conformance and compatibility tests.
Pass authorization-denial, malformed-input, isolation, timeout, cancellation, retry/idempotency and audit-provenance tests.
Run a small end-to-end task on pinned SHAs and capture Run ID, Job ID, Step ID, exit code and terminal logs.
Keep implementation status unverified until the above evidence exists.
residuals: No implemented Aurora-to-Genesis adapter is established by the inspected source files.
Aurora runtime tool_executor and sandbox are explicitly PLANNED in the inspected component plan.
Genesis WorkflowEngine is an in-process Python API; no remote/IPC contract was identified in inspected files.
Transport, concrete request/response schemas, identity propagation, capability enforcement and runtime lifecycle remain undecided.
Source mapping is partial: candidate workflow and artifact symbols are identified, but complete manifests, callers, tests and adapter conformance remain to be inspected.
No end-to-end exact-SHA verification has been run for Aurora invoking a Genesis workflow.

findings.finding: Aurora is documented as AI services/agents/inference/runtime integration and explicitly not ShivaCore TCB.
agent_runtime.atc, tool_executor.atc and sandbox/task scheduler/result collector are marked PLANNED; no request/response contract is specified in this plan.
Engine owns runtime/simulation/editor/build/SDK/Franchise Factory; provider and chain/VM integrations remain explicit boundaries.
Factory documents 17 provider-neutral workflows and says external providers and engine adapters are injected boundaries; production adapters remain unproven.

Source contains WorkflowRegistry, WorkflowEngine.run(workflow_id, payload, executor), stage-based injected Executor, and workflow definitions. This is a concrete candidate integration seam, not a remotely callable API.
Source contains ArtifactRef, ArtifactEnvelope, ArtifactContractError and validate_artifact; suitable for typed artifact/provenance mapping, but not itself an Aurora transport contract.
